old: This word grew out of a past-tense form describing something that had been outfitted with weapons.
In Spanish, this word simply means "fleet" or "navy."
It shares a Latin ancestor with the English word army.
clues: This noun for a large, imposing group comes from a Latin verb meaning to equip someone with weapons.
Today it names a huge fleet of warships, far grander and more menacing than an ordinary fleet, and English took it straight from the Spanish word for a navy.
Its sibling word is army, born from the same Latin root. People also use it loosely for any vast advancing crowd, such as a whole sea of drones or fishing boats.
